cands.bio: Republican Speaker of the Alabama House of Representatives since January 2023. He has represented District 24 since 2014 and was House majority leader from 2017. Former Rainsville city councilman and mayor, newspaper owner, and longtime Sand Mountain Electric Cooperative employee.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Nathaniel Ledbetter was born or when, if ever, he moved to Alabama. The pages we reviewed show no specific votes, bills or public statements on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He has said immigration and violent crime were priorities for the 2025 session, but the source gives no detail on the positions. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey.

qual.background: State House member since 2014, majority leader 2017–2022 and Speaker since 2023. Earlier he served on the Rainsville City Council, was mayor of Rainsville until 2002, owned a newspaper and worked over 30 years for an electric cooperative.
qual.why: He has 12 years of legislative service and chamber leadership as majority leader and Speaker, plus local elected office as mayor and a business and management background.
